intuition.text: A courier can climb to a concourse without leaning its whole movement model uphill. Keep the height needed to place its feet in the level, while describing its facing with a compass direction. The route’s elevation and the character’s orientation answer different questions.
intuition.situation: An upright courier crosses a ramp to a raised concourse. Its feet gain height, but its body has no need to pitch or roll with the ramp.

example.name: The raised-concourse courier
example.description: The courier follows a straight plan route to ({targetX}, {targetZ}) in x/z, with a speed limit of {maxSpeed} units/s and acceleration limit of {maxAcceleration} units/s². A surface starts rising at x = {rampStart}, gains {rise} units over a run of {rampRun} units and supplies height after each {timeStep} s plan step. The profile and plan show the same courier. Its facing has yaw only; the final partial plan step is clamped and stopped for this teaching example.

steps.title: Steer in the ground plane
steps.text: Map world x/z into the public scene engine’s Vec2 coordinates and call Seek. Height is still stored, but it is not an input to that planar steering rule. A {maxAcceleration} units/s² budget is shared across the plan direction rather than applied independently to both axes.

steps.title: Move the plan position
steps.text: Use the engine’s vector operations to add acceleration over {timeStep} s and cap plan speed at {maxSpeed} units/s. Move using that velocity. A local final-step clamp ends this straight route exactly at the target; it is not a gradual Arrive behaviour.

steps.title: Resolve height from the surface
steps.text: The local sampler assigns height from the updated x position: below the ramp, up its linear rise, or on the concourse. The current foot height is {height}; its observed vertical rate is {verticalSpeed} units/s. The sampler is deliberately separate from steering and proves neither ground contact nor traversability.

steps.title: Keep facing upright
steps.text: Derive yaw from the plan velocity and retain it when stopped. Pitch and roll stay at {pitch}° and {roll}° even as height changes. The model therefore has a spatial position without needing a free aircraft pose. An upright line in the profile makes that restriction visible.

pseudocode.ordinary:
plan = Vec2(position.x, position.z)
planTarget = Vec2(targetX, targetZ)
acceleration = engine.seek(planBody, planTarget)

candidateVelocity = engine.clipLength(velocity + acceleration * dt, maxSpeed)
travel = candidateVelocity * dt
if length(travel) >= distance(plan, planTarget):
  plan = planTarget; velocity = zero2  // local final-step clamp
else:
  plan += travel; velocity = candidateVelocity

nextHeight = localSurfaceHeight(plan.x, rampStart, rampRun, rise)
verticalSpeed = (nextHeight - position.height) / dt
position = (plan.x, nextHeight, plan.y)

if length(candidateVelocity) > 0:
  yaw = atan2(candidateVelocity.y, candidateVelocity.x)
pitch = 0; roll = 0
drawPlanAndUprightProfile(position, yaw)

visual.textEquivalent: At {seconds} s the same courier appears in plan at ({x}, {z}) and in profile with foot height {height}; its plan speed is {speed} units/s, height rate {verticalSpeed} units/s, yaw {yaw}°, pitch {pitch}° and roll {roll}°, so the profile body remains upright.

implementations.relevance: Godot’s public platformer demo is a grounded character controller in a spatial world. It shows how horizontal facing can remain upright while vertical motion is handled separately.
implementations.explanation: The controller separates horizontal velocity from vertical velocity, handles gravity and jumps, then combines them for move_and_slide. Its grounded mesh-facing calculation removes the up component and builds a basis with Vector3.UP fixed. The root moves through the spatial level while grounded facing turns within the horizontal plane.

implementations.project: Recast Navigation · Detour crowd and path corridor
implementations.relevance: Detour provides ground navigation and crowd movement on a navigation mesh. It implements the surface-position part of this representation and leaves rendered facing to the caller.
implementations.explanation: Crowd steering clears the vertical component of its path direction. The path corridor then moves a proposed spatial position along the navigation surface and replaces its height with getPolyHeight. Polygon connectivity constrains that adjustment; it is more than assigning height from a global function. These files do not prescribe a yaw-only rendered pose.

limits: A height sampler can conceal an impossible climb. Changing only the ramp run to {ledgeRun} makes a ledge, yet the courier still receives its new height in a single step. The comparison exposes the resulting vertical-rate spike; a collision or navigation controller must judge that transition.

This particular surface sampler assigns one height to each x position. It cannot distinguish a bridge deck from a passage below it. A spatial position plus an appropriate surface or navigation layer is needed; the yaw-only choice does not require such a limited height sampler.
The courier has no gravity, jump arc, contact response or gradual braking here. The final-step stop and sampled height are explicit local teaching rules.
An aircraft or swimming character that must point its nose uphill or roll independently needs a richer pose. Raising the courier’s height alone cannot provide those rotations.

nearby.why: Use the flat movement model when the courier’s level has no height that changes movement or placement.
Use full volume movement when a flying or swimming actor needs height in steering and pitch or roll in its pose.
Read Jumping when the courier must cross the ledge with a take-off and landing rather than receive an instantaneous sampled height.
